intro: You are standing at Gordion, a mound in Ankara province whose story begins in the 3rd millennium BC. This was the capital of Phrygia, home of the Midas tumulus and of the legend of the Gordian Knot.
history: Gordion was the seat of the Phrygian kings, at its peak under Midas in the 8th century BC. And it was here that Alexander cut the knot that promised rule over Asia.
structure-1: Now look at the Midas Tumulus, one of Anatolia's largest burial mounds. It is attributed to the Phrygian king Midas himself.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the King's Gate, the megaron buildings and the fortification system.
facts: Did you know? The Midas tumulus contains the oldest standing wooden chamber in the world. The Gordian Knot was here too, in the city's temple, with its prophecy that whoever untied it would rule Asia — and Alexander cut it with his sword. And residues in the cauldrons of the burial chamber have been analysed: the funeral feast was washed down with a drink of honey, grape and barley.
outro: This brings our tour of Gordion to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water. The kings of Phrygia bid you farewell. Enjoy your visit.
